To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

svm based survival models using regression constraints outperform svm based models using ranking constraints, but the latter have the advantage of a theoretical link to standard statistical models for the analysis of time-to-event data.

svm based models for survival analysis based on regression constraints perform significantly and consistently better than svm based methods based on ranking constraints and that svm based methods including both ranking and regression perform significantly better on clinical datasets than methods based on regression constraints only, while on high dimensional datasets, the performance of the two approaches is comparable.
svm based survival models using regression constraints have a comparable or better performance than models using ranking constraints.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new models for survival data and their evaluation in terms of their performance.
the development of new models for survival data based on machine learning techniques.
the development of a svm model for survival data which is theoretically sound and has a good predictive performance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the best performance is obtained with a combination of ranking and regression constraints.

svm based survival models including regression constraints perform significantly superior to ranking only models, but the inclusion of ranking constraints in the optimization problem is important to make a theoretical link with existing statistical models for survival analysis.
svm based survival models including regression constraints perform best on all datasets.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

svm based methods for survival analysis using regression constraints should be preferred to methods based on ranking constraints and that the inclusion of ranking constraints can improve the model performance.
the ranking approach is more suitable for clinical data and the regression approach for high-dimensional data.
svm based methods including ranking and regression constraints are the best performing models, and that these models have a clear link with existing models for survival data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the inclusion of regression constraints is a key ingredient for the performance of svm based survival analysis.
svm based models are competitive to classical statistical models for survival analysis.
the ranking approach is not a suitable method to deal with survival data.
